This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment

Heard Sri.P.Mahadevaswamy, learned counsel for the appellants and also Smt.Manjula.N.Tejaswi,
learned counsel for respondent No.1.
2.

The father, mother and the elder sister of the deceased Kishore moved an application claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- in total on the ground that the deceased Kishore (herein after referred to as the 'deceased' for brevity) died in the road traffic accident that occurred on 24.02.2020 and that the accident occurred NC: 2024:KHC:32494 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of respondent No.2.
The Tribunal deciding the aspect of negligence held that the deceased was also responsible for the accident to occur along with the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.TN-88-B-5193.
Also the Tribunal gave a finding that the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry compared to the negligence which the deceased contributed is in the ratio of 70:30.
3. Learned counsel Sri.P.Mahadevaswamy did not argue much on the aspect of negligence attributed on the part of the deceased.
The submission of the learned counsel revolved around the income of the deceased as assessed by the Tribunal and the ultimate amount awarded as compensation.
4. Learned counsel Sri.P.Mahadevaswamy contends that the deceased as a driver was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal for the purpose of calculating compensation took the notional income of the deceased as Rs.11,000/- p.m. which is unjustifiable.

sentences.text:
2 Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as Rs.14,500/- p.m. that too in respect of persons whose occupation is not established, but in the case on hand, the deceased as driver was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. and therefore, the said aspect ought to have been considered by the Tribunal.
5.
Opposing the said submission, learned counsel for respondent No.1 Smt.Manjula.N.Tejaswi contends that neither the occupation nor the income were established before the Tribunal.
Learned counsel states that production of driving license does not mean that the occupation and the income are established.
Learned counsel states that as no proof is produced with regard to the occupation and income, the Tribunal rightly took the notional income as Rs.11,000/- p.m. which needs no interference.
6. The entire case is that the deceased while driving a mini bus met with an accident when the said mini NC: 2024:KHC:32494 bus dashed against rear portion of the lorry.
It is not in dispute that the deceased was holding license to drive the said vehicle.
Thus it is established that the deceased holding driving license was driving the mini bus at the time of accident.

Though Smt.Manjula.N.Tejaswi contended that the driving license of the deceased was not produced, no evidence is led by the insurance company that the deceased without valid driving license was driving a minibus.
Thus taking into consideration all these facts, this Court is of the view that the notional income of the deceased has to be taken as Rs.17,000/- p.m.
There is no denial of the fact that deceased was aged about 21 years by the date of accident and that he died as a bachelor.

Thus the deduction towards personal and living expenses should be 50% as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104.

sentences.text:
In the decision that is rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case,
there is a clear mention that the amount that is liable to be awarded towards funeral expenses, loss of estate and loss of consortium is required to be increased by 10% for every three years.
Admittedly, the accident occurred in the year 2020.

Thus the appellants are entitled to Rs.16,500/-
towards funeral NC: 2024:KHC:32494 expenses, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate.
The appellant Nos.1 and 2 are also entitled for Rs.44,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.

8. Thus, the compensation which the appellants are entitled to under each head is as under:
 Sl.
Description Amount  No  1 Loss of dependency Rs.25,70,400  2 Funeral expenses Rs.16,500  3 Loss of estate Rs.16,500  4 Loss of Rs.44,000
Total Rs.26,47,400

9. Out of the sum granted i.e., Rs.26,47,400/- the liability in respect of the respondents would be 70% of it i.e., Rs.18,53,180/-.
10.

Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2024:KHC:32494 (ii) The compensation which the appellants are entitled to from the respondents is Rs.18,53,180/-.
(iii) The awarded sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(v) The apportionment made remains undisturbed.
